0:
cache:
  enabled: true
  dir: /data/cache
  port: 8088
  proxy_port: 8089
container:
  docker_host: "-"
  workdir_parent: shared/workdir
host:
  workdir_parent: /data/act
kubernetes:
  namespace: forgejo
  poll_timeout: 10m
log:
  level: info
plugins:
  k8s:
    address: "unix:///plugin/forgejo-runner-k8s.sock"
    options:
      namespace: forgejo
      poll_timeout: 10m
      labels: "app.kubernetes.io/name=forgejo-runner-instance,egress.home.arpa/custom-egress=true"
      resources: |
        requests:
          cpu: 100m
          memory: 256Mi
        limits:
          memory: 1Gi
runner:
  capacity: 3
  labels:
    - ubuntu-latest:k8s:/config/podspec-default.yaml
    - default:k8s:/config/podspec-default.yaml
    - docker:k8s:/config/podspec-dind.yaml
    - multiarch:k8s:/config/podspec-dind.yaml  # you need binfmt-misc extension for multiarch
  timeout: 3h
  shutdown_timeout: 3m

containers:
  - env:
      - name: DEBIAN_FRONTEND
        value: noninteractive
    image: ghcr.io/bjw-s-labs/forgejo-runner:ubuntu-24.04@sha256:fce99eeccdfec1780643510c72d8fcbb8ef5fa82a54066ed4aaab3d03a3eb830
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: main
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 1Gi
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 4Gi
nodeSelector:
  kubernetes.io/hostname: kharkiv
restartPolicy: Never

initContainers:
  - name: dind
    image: docker:29-dind
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    restartPolicy: Always
    env:
      - name: DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR
        value: /certs
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 1Gi
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 8Gi
    volumeMounts:
      - name: docker-storage
        mountPath: /var/lib/docker
      - name: docker-certs
        mountPath: /certs
    startupProbe:
      exec:
        command:
          - sh
          - -c
          - docker --tlsverify --tlscacert=/certs/client/ca.pem --tlscert=/certs/client/cert.pem --tlskey=/certs/client/key.pem -H tcp://localhost:2376 info
      initialDelaySeconds: 5
      periodSeconds: 1
      failureThreshold: 30
containers:
  - env:
      - name: DEBIAN_FRONTEND
        value: noninteractive
      - name: DOCKER_HOST
        value: tcp://localhost:2376
      - name: DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY
        value: "1"
      - name: DOCKER_CERT_PATH
        value: /certs/client
    image: ghcr.io/bjw-s-labs/forgejo-runner:ubuntu-24.04@sha256:fce99eeccdfec1780643510c72d8fcbb8ef5fa82a54066ed4aaab3d03a3eb830
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: main
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 1Gi
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 4Gi
    volumeMounts:
      - name: docker-certs
        mountPath: /certs
        readOnly: true
volumes:
  - name: docker-storage
    emptyDir: {}
  - name: docker-certs
    emptyDir: {}
nodeSelector:
  kubernetes.io/hostname: kharkiv
restartPolicy: Never

echo "🚀 Starting Offsite Sync to Google Drive..."

cp /config-ro/rclone.conf /tmp/rclone.conf
chmod 600 /tmp/rclone.conf

rclone sync /data/backups/homeassistant gdrive:homeassistant-backups \
  --transfers 16 \
  --checkers 16 \
  --fast-list \
  --delete-after \
  --log-level INFO \
  --stats 1m \
  --retries 3
echo "✅ Offsite Sync Complete!"

[couchdb]
single_node=true
max_document_size = 50000000

[chttpd]
require_valid_user_except_for_up = true
max_http_request_size = 4294967296
enable_cors = true

[chttpd_auth]
require_valid_user = true

[httpd]
WWW-Authenticate = Basic realm="couchdb"
bind_address = 0.0.0.0

[cors]
credentials = true
headers = accept, authorization, content-type, origin, referer
methods = GET, PUT, POST, HEAD, DELETE
origins = app://obsidian.md, capacitor://localhost, http://localhost

/hr/quay.io-jetstack-charts-cert-manager.title: cert-manager helm release
/hr/quay.io-jetstack-charts-cert-manager.name: cert-manager
/hr/quay.io-jetstack-charts-cert-manager.doc: cert-manager is a certificate management controller for Kubernetes. It automates the management and issuance of TLS certificates from various issuing sources. It will ensure certificates are valid and up to date periodically, and attempt to renew certificates at an appropriate time before expiry.

/hr/quay.io-cilium-charts-cilium-cilium-.title: cilium helm release
/hr/quay.io-cilium-charts-cilium-cilium-.name: cilium
/hr/quay.io-cilium-charts-cilium-cilium-.doc: Cilium is a networking, security, and observability solution for Kubernetes, built on eBPF. It provides high-performance networking with support for Layer 3-7 policies, load balancing, and transparent encryption. With Cilium, you can enforce fine-grained security policies, observe network flows in real time, and integrate seamlessly with service meshes. It also offers eBPF-powered network policies and cluster mesh capabilities, enabling secure communication across multiple Kubernetes clusters.
